newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech c.bank says mkt will determine repo rate.
newsitem.headline: Czech c.bank says mkt will determine repo rate.

text.p: The Czech National Bank (CNB) on Thursday said it had not set a target for how much it would raise its repo rates, and that market conditions would be the determining factor.
"The repo rates will now be adjusted according to the market. We have no target right now," CNB spokesman Martin Svehla told Reuters.
Earlier on Thursday the CNB said in a statement that it would raise its repo rates and make their usage flexible as of May 16.
The statement gave no further details and Svehla declined to elaborate. The repo rate currently stands at 12.4 percent, while the reverse repo rate stands at 12.6 percent.
The CNB holds repo tenders to either supply or drain liquidity from the market almost daily.

The announcement came after the crown plunged to a record low of five percent on the depreciation side of its dollar/mark basket parity, prompting the CNB to intervene on the market to support the currency for the first time in over a year.
In late afternoon trading the crown was holding steady, but a little weaker than in the early afternoon, at about 3.4-3.6 percent on the depreciation side of basket parity.
